BiblicalUsage: Chanukka in Aramaic is dedication, and Daniel uses it for the wrong kind. Nebuchadnezzar gathered the princes and rulers to the dedication of the golden image he had set up, and they stood before it. Ezra uses the same word for the right kind: the children of Israel kept the dedication of the house of God with joy, offering a hundred bullocks and two hundred rams.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two dedications stand as a warning and a pattern. One image is dedicated by a king who demands worship, and the other house is dedicated by a people who offer joyfully. I hold that what is dedicated tells you who is worshipped, and the difference between the two could not be sharper.
